title: The Promises and Pitfalls of LLM Annotations in Dataset Labeling: a Case Study on Media Bias Detection
measurement_description: Invariance of media bias detection models to substitutions of religious figures (e.g., Buddha, Christ) as part of a 'prejudice test' within a broader behavioral stress-testing framework (CheckList).
findings: In a prejudice invariance test, the model trained on human labels (HA-FT) was slightly more robust (89.5% success rate) to the substitution of religious figures (Buddha, Christ) than the model trained on synthetic LLM-generated labels (SA-FT, 85.2% success rate).
references: Meysam Alizadeh, Maël Kubli, Zeynab Samei, Shirin Dehghani, Juan Diego Bermeo, Maria Korobeynikova, and Fabrizio Gilardi. 2023. Open-Source Large Language Models Outperform Crowd Workers and Approach ChatGPT in Text-Annotation Tasks. Computation and Language, (arXiv:2307.02179).
